page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance family cloud server configured with 12 shared vCPUs mapped from 6 physical Intel Xeon cores utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server consistently in the average tier across standard compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1189.0 and a multi-core score of 8081.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88. In data processing tasks, the system demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 11.99 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 18.53 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 1224.9 GB/sec for cached reads, dropping to 87.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.62 GB/sec for uncached writes.

While the server handles lightweight machine learning tasks adequately, processing 719.57 tokens per second for a small 135M parameter LLM, it exhibits significant performance degradation on larger models. Prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to a poor 16.55 tokens per second, and text generation falls to a weak 7.43 tokens per second, with no capability for 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU allocation, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and intermediate database operations.
description: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is an x86_64 High Performance cloud server featuring 12 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 24.0 GB of RAM and a 500 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the average tier for general compute, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 8081.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 17934.88. It delivers solid data throughput, including 11.99 GB/sec in static web serving and 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of GPU acceleration limit its utility for demanding AI workloads, where LLM inference on 7B models drops to a weak 7.43 tokens per second. This server represents a balanced, qualitatively cost-effective option for multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, web serving, and general-purpose database operations.
